name: Originate and structure direct deals
summary: Account executives sell leases and loans directly to established businesses, mostly larger mid-ticket deals. For each opportunity they learn what the customer wants to buy, check the existing relationship, collect a supplier quote and financial statements, structure the term, residual and payment pattern, get used equipment valued and non-standard rates priced, present a proposal and, if the customer accepts, submit a signed application with a deal summary to credit. Most elapsed time goes on waiting for customers' accountants, valuations and deal desk pricing, and customers compare offers from their banks while they wait; re-keying from the CRM into the origination portal and a thin sales support team add delay and errors.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size independent Canadian equipment lessor with 14 direct account executives, a small sales support team, a CRM for the pipeline and a separate origination portal for credit submissions.
baseline.notes: An opportunity starts at the first serious conversation about a purchase; prospecting that never reaches one is not counted.

trigger: A business customer asks to finance equipment, a supplier or existing customer refers a purchase, or an account executive's prospecting turns up one.
end_state: A signed credit application with its package and deal summary is submitted to credit, or the opportunity is closed as not qualified, not pursued, stalled or lost to another lender.

volume.seasonality: Busier in spring for construction and agricultural equipment and before the calendar year-end, when customers buy for capital cost allowance; 2020 fell in the spring.

evidence.note: Process map figure; with about 64% of opportunities becoming applications it matches the organisation file's 480 direct applications a month.
Duties of lenders' business sales officers are documented; FTE is the author's estimate from step times and the organisation file's 750 opportunities a month.
Sales support analysts chase documents and key applications for the account executives. FTE from step times; 4 in the organisation file.
The direct sales manager endorses pricing requests and reviews large submissions. Author estimate.

systems.name: Customer relationship management system (partner accounts, pipeline, commissions data)
Vendor and broker application portal with origination workflow and document generation
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Document imaging and contract file store

steps.name: Log the opportunity and hold the first conversation
steps.description: The account executive logs a new opportunity in the CRM, from a customer call, a supplier referral, a repeat customer or their own prospecting, and talks to the owner or finance manager about the equipment, its cost and supplier, timing, the business and its current lenders.

error.defect_description: Equipment, cost or timing recorded wrongly in the CRM.

evidence.note: Interviewing business applicants and learning their needs is documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Look up the existing relationship and exposure
steps.description: A sales support analyst searches the lease system and CRM for the customer and related companies: active contracts, payment history, total exposure, recent declines and open applications, and notes the result on the opportunity.

error.defect_description: A related company's exposure is missed.

evidence.note: Exposure checks before structuring are common practice; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Qualify the opportunity
steps.description: The account executive weighs the opportunity against the credit appetite and their pipeline: industry, time in business, equipment type and age, deal size and the existing exposure. They decide to pursue it with a meeting, handle it by phone, or turn it away early.

control.basis: Credit policy target market: industries, equipment types, minimum time in business and maximum exposure the company finances

next.condition: new or mid-ticket customer worth a meeting
outside appetite or not a real purchase

evidence.note: Evaluating applicants' standing is documented; most customers are small and mid-sized businesses. Shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Meet the customer and review the equipment's purpose
steps.description: For larger or new customers the account executive visits the site or holds a video meeting with the owner, sees the operation and the equipment's purpose, and discusses how the business earns money and how it wants to pay.

evidence.note: Structuring to the client's needs is documented; meeting share, travel and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Request the equipment quote and financial information
steps.description: The account executive emails the customer a list of what is needed: the supplier's quote with model, year and serial details, the last two year-end financial statements and interims for larger deals, tax returns where statements are not reviewed, and personal net worth statements for guarantors of young businesses.

error.defect_description: Document list is incomplete, so a second request is needed.

evidence.note: Package contents and the $80,000 financial statement threshold are stated in the sources.

steps.name: Customer gathers the quote, statements and tax returns
steps.description: The customer asks the supplier for a formal quote and its accountant for statements and interims, and sends them by email. Interims and statements for related companies often take the longest.

next.condition: customer drops the purchase or uses its bank

evidence.note: Waiting for accountant-prepared statements is the usual delay; durations are author estimates.

steps.name: Chase the customer for missing documents
steps.description: The sales support analyst emails and phones the customer or its accountant for the missing items, keeps the CRM task open and tells the account executive when an opportunity has stalled.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Check the package for completeness
steps.description: The sales support analyst checks that the quote matches the equipment discussed, that statements cover the right years and are signed or accountant-prepared, that interims are recent, and that guarantor details are there. Gaps go back to the customer.

control.basis: Credit policy documentation requirements: two year-ends plus interims above the application-only limit, guarantor net worth statements for young businesses

evidence.note: Required package items, and bank statements or financials for larger approvals, are documented; the gap rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Structure the lease or loan
steps.description: The account executive chooses lease or loan, term, residual or purchase option, down payment and any seasonal or skip payments that fit the customer's cash cycle and tax position, and runs payment options from the rate card in the pricing spreadsheet. They decide whether the deal needs a valuation or non-standard pricing.

error.defect_description: Structure breaks a guideline, for example a term too long for the asset or a residual above the table.

next.condition: used or specialised equipment needs a valuation
rate below the card needed to win

evidence.note: Seasonal schedules, deferred payments and the lease tax rules that shape structure are documented; shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Request an equipment valuation
steps.description: The account executive sends asset management a valuation request with the equipment description, year, hours or kilometres, serial numbers, photos and the proposed term and residual.

error.defect_description: Hours, year or options missing, so asset management asks again.

control.basis: Credit policy: used, specialised or high-value equipment needs an asset management valuation before the residual and advance are set

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Update the structure with the valuation
steps.description: When asset management returns its value, sometimes after a third-party desktop or on-site appraisal, the account executive resets the advance and residual and decides whether the deal still works at standard pricing.

next.condition: value too low for the deal

evidence.note: Third-party appraisal turnaround of 7 to 15 business days desktop and 15 to 25 on site sets the high end; internal valuations take a few days. Shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare a pricing request for the deal desk
steps.description: The account executive writes up the requested rate, structure, competing offer, expected yield and the relationship's value, and attaches the payment model.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Sales manager endorses the pricing request
steps.description: The manager of direct sales checks that the concession is needed and worth it for the relationship, then forwards the request to the deal desk or sends it back to be restructured.

control.basis: Pricing authority matrix: the sales manager endorses any rate below the rate card floor before the deal desk prices it

next.condition: endorsed and sent to the deal desk

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Apply the deal desk's answer
steps.description: When the deal desk replies with an approved rate, fees and structure or a refusal, the account executive updates the payment options and decides whether the deal can still win.

next.condition: customer took another offer while waiting

evidence.note: Deal desk turnaround is an author estimate.

steps.name: Present the proposal to the customer
steps.description: The account executive sends or walks through a proposal letter with payment options, end-of-term choices, fees and conditions, noting that it is subject to credit approval.

evidence.note: Structure options offered to the customer are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Customer compares offers and decides
steps.description: The customer compares the proposal with its bank's or other lessors' terms, often asking for a sharper rate or a different payment pattern.

evidence.note: Customers weigh rates, flexibility and turnaround; shares and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Obtain the signed credit application and consents
steps.description: The account executive sends the credit application by e-mail or e-signature and gets it back signed by the business and each guarantor, with consent to obtain credit reports and share information with credit and funders.

error.defect_description: A guarantor's consent or signature is missing.

control.basis: PIPEDA principle 4.3 (consent): signed consent from the business and each guarantor before credit reports are obtained and information is shared with credit

evidence.note: Meaningful consent before collecting and disclosing personal information is required; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Key the application into the origination portal
steps.description: The sales support analyst re-keys the customer, owners, guarantors, equipment, supplier and structure from the CRM and spreadsheet into the origination portal and attaches the statements, quote, valuation and any pricing approval.

error.defect_description: Owner, equipment or structure keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Completing credit documentation is a documented duty; re-keying between the CRM and the portal and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Write the deal summary for credit
steps.description: The account executive writes a cover note for the analyst: the business and its owners, the purpose of the equipment, why this structure, strengths and risks, and the relationship's history and potential.

error.defect_description: A known weakness is left out of the summary.

evidence.note: Submitting applications with recommendations is a documented duty; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Manager reviews a large or unusual submission
steps.description: The direct sales manager reads the summary and structure for large deals and policy exceptions, asks for changes where the deal will struggle in credit and releases it.

control.basis: Sales management review of submissions above $500,000 or with policy exceptions

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Submit to credit and confirm to the customer
steps.description: The sales support analyst submits the application to the credit queue in the portal, closes the CRM stage and emails the customer that the application is with credit and when to expect an answer.

evidence.note: Underwriting is separate from origination, so sales hands the file to credit; times are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Customer's statements do not arrive
exceptions.description: The customer or its accountant is slow to send statements or interims; sales support chases and some opportunities stall and close.

exceptions.name: Used or specialised equipment needs a valuation
exceptions.description: Asset management values the equipment, sometimes through a third-party appraiser, before the residual and advance can be set.

exceptions.name: Rate below the rate card to beat a bank
exceptions.description: The account executive asks for a sharper rate; the sales manager endorses it and the deal desk prices it before the proposal goes out.

exceptions.name: Customer asks for a different structure
exceptions.description: After the proposal the customer wants seasonal payments, a different residual or a shorter term, so the deal is restructured.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from first conversation to application submitted or opportunity closed, all outcomes
benchmarks.population: Author estimate for direct equipment finance sales at a Canadian independent lessor

evidence.note: Built from customer document waits of days to weeks and appraisal times of 7 to 25 business days for the minority of deals that need one; no published direct-origination cycle time was found.

benchmarks.unit: CAD deal size from which two years of statements plus interims are required
share of opportunities submitted to credit
benchmarks.population: This organisation file (480 direct applications from 750 opportunities a month)

evidence.note: Ratio of two organisation file estimates.

pain_points.description: Waiting for customers' accountants to send year-end statements and interims is the longest delay and many opportunities stall there.

evidence.note: Statement requirements are documented; the delay is an author assessment.

pain_points.description: Valuations and deal desk pricing add days while the customer holds a bank offer.

evidence.note: Appraisal turnaround is documented; the loss effect is an author assessment.

pain_points.description: The deal lives in the CRM and spreadsheets and is re-keyed into the origination portal, causing errors that credit intake catches.

evidence.note: Author assessment of separate CRM and origination systems in the organisation file.

pain_points.description: Account executives split their time between prospecting, structuring, paperwork and post-decision follow-up, so hands-on time per deal is squeezed.

evidence.note: Author assessment from the staffing check.

sources.title: NOC 2021 profile 63102: Financial sales representatives
sources.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada (National Occupational Classification)
sources.supports: Main duties include interviewing applicants for business loans, researching and evaluating the applicant's financial status, references, credit and ability to repay, submitting credit applications with recommendations, completing credit documentation and proposing solutions for objectives such as business expansion; example titles include credit officer and commercial banking accounts officer.

sources.title: Equipment leasing over $250,000
sources.supports: Above $250,000 a lessor asks for a company overview of up to two pages, a write-up of the equipment's purpose and financial justification, the last two year-end financial statements and current interims, two years of tax returns unless statements are audited or reviewed, statements on principals owning 20% or more and a list of current loans and leases; once the package is in place an answer typically comes within a business day; deferred payments, longer amortisations and seasonal schedules are available.

sources.title: EasyLease: equipment and vendor leasing
sources.supports: Canadian leasing: businesses under two years old are limited to $70,000 and must provide a personal guarantee and personal net worth statement; transactions of $80,000 and up need two years of financial statements plus interims; applications turn around in 24 to 48 hours; customised payment schedules (seasonal leases) are offered.

sources.title: Equipment appraisals
sources.supports: Lender-specific equipment appraisals take 7 to 15 business days desktop and 15 to 25 business days on site, on fair market value, orderly liquidation value and forced liquidation value premises; rush service is available.

sources.title: PIPEDA fair information principle 3: consent
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Meaningful consent is an essential element of PIPEDA; organisations generally need meaningful consent before collecting, using or disclosing personal information, and express consent when the information is sensitive.

sources.title: Equipment financing for businesses
sources.supports: A Canadian lender's equipment finance process: the client selects the equipment and contacts a financing expert, and the lender structures the lease or loan to the client's needs and coordinates with a dealer to deliver the equipment; lease features include structured payments, purchase options and trade-ups across agriculture, construction, forestry, health care, manufacturing, mining and transportation.

sources.title: Marlin Business Services Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2019
sources.publisher: Marlin Business Services Corp. via US SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Each relationship has an assigned sales account executive handling pricing, credit, documentation, training and marketing matters; credit underwriting is performed and managed separately from origination.

sources.title: Asset-based finance in Canada: the 2019-2020 year (Canadian Market Overview)
sources.supports: Business customers choosing a leasing company value funding rates and affordability, reaching someone to solve an issue, customer service, turnaround time, information requirements, flexibility and consistency in credit decisions; trucks, trailers and computers are the equipment most likely to be acquired.

sources.title: Equipment financing credit guidelines (dealers and vendors)
sources.supports: Larger deals may need tax returns, interim financials, personal financial statements or a debt schedule; weaker credit is offset with a down payment or extra collateral; application-only requests are often decided in 24 to 48 hours.

sources.title: Asset/equipment finance and leasing (Canada)
sources.supports: About 60% of the Canadian leasing industry's customers are small and medium-sized businesses; the specified leasing property rules split the market into small-ticket leasing of exempt assets with full capital cost allowance for the lessor and other assets where the lessor's tax benefit is limited; lessees of non-exempt assets can elect under section 16.1 to treat rent as principal and interest.

sources.title: Applying for financing (help centre)
sources.supports: Approval above pre-approved amounts may require recent bank statements or financial information; the sales representative is the customer's contact through the application.

assumptions: The case starts at the first serious conversation about a purchase. Prospecting calls, events and supplier visits that do not produce an opportunity are outside this workflow, although they take a real share of account executives' time.
About 60% of opportunities end in an application in the simulation (about 450 a month), close to the organisation file's 480 direct applications from 750 opportunities.

About 22% of opportunities send a pricing request to the deal desk (about 165 a month of the deal desk's 350) and about 10% send a valuation request to asset management (about 75 a month of its 280). Pricing approvals and valuations return into open cases, so their trigger share is 0.

Hands-on times are lean. The organisation file gives 14 account executives about 750 opportunities and 480 applications a month, about 34 applications each, which is high for mid-ticket work. With about 10.3 FTE here and 3.2 FTE in communicate-credit-decisions, account executives are close to fully used; a desk doing mostly mid-ticket deals would usually need more people or fewer, larger deals.
Sales support analysts (about 3.5 of 4) chase documents and key applications; the manager spends a little over half of the role on endorsements and reviews.
No anti-money-laundering identification is done here: non-bank lessors were not reporting entities in 2019-2022 (organisation file assumption). Identity and bureau checks happen in credit intake.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
External steps have zero touch time; customer and supplier time is in wait_before_min.
